page: Amazon Web Services m8gn.16xlarge is a general-purpose, network-optimized server instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features 64 dedicated physical cores on the 64-bit ARMv9 architecture, utilizing AWS Neoverse-V2 processors running at 2.8 GHz. The instance is equipped with 256.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, relying instead on network-attached storage and a high-speed 200 Gbps baseline network interface.

In benchmark evaluations, the m8gn.16xlarge demonstrates top-tier multi-core and memory subsystem performance. Multi-threaded operations, such as bzip3 decompression and software compilation with Clang, rank in the top 10% of tested systems. Memory bandwidth is a key strength, with cached read-only speeds reaching 7390.11 GB/sec and uncached write speeds at 235.58 GB/sec. Database operations and Redis SET performance are exceptionally strong, processing 140.57 million operations per second. However, single-core performance and small-model LLM text generation are relatively average, indicating a tradeoff where workload efficiency is heavily dependent on parallelization.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ARM-based architecture provides high resource density and exceptional memory throughput per unit of resource, making it highly competitive for parallelized workloads without the premium of traditional x86 architectures. The instance is highly suited for high-throughput web serving, database hosting, large-scale software compilation, and multi-threaded data processing tasks that can leverage its 200 Gbps network bandwidth and dedicated 64-core execution environment.
